subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` keys that look like credentials be allowed into skill-owned host `exec` subprocesses, and how should that interact with generic `exec` secret stripping?
rationale: The current code violates the documented host skill-env behavior for real users, but a broad fix changes when credential values enter executable child processes and can conflict with active hardening against skill secret leakage into unrelated generic `exec`.

options.title: Allow only skill-scoped exec env
options.body: Permit user-configured per-skill env keys for that skill's own host exec context while keeping dangerous env names blocked and stripping skill secrets from unrelated generic exec children.

options.title: Require metadata declarations
options.body: Keep credential-shaped configured names blocked unless the skill manifest declares them, then update the `gog` skill or its ClawHub package metadata and docs accordingly.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Document that credential-shaped `skills.entries.<skill>.env` names are intentionally blocked and require top-level/system env or sandbox-specific env configuration.

recommendation.title: Allow only skill-scoped exec env
recommendation.body: Permit user-configured per-skill env keys for that skill's own host exec context while keeping dangerous env names blocked and stripping skill secrets from unrelated generic exec children.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses documented skills behavior, host env hardening, and credential-to-exec security policy, where this history has the strongest cross-surface signal.
